title: BPSC TRE 4.0 Day 01 High-Yield Practice Test

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: What is the correct grammatical Sandhi-Vichhed (disjunction) of the Sanskrit loanword 'Ujjwal' (उज्ज्वल)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct Sandhi-Vichhed is 'Ut + Jwal' (उत् + ज्वल = उज्ज्वल).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Consonant Sandhi (Vyanjan Sandhi) Rule: When 't' (त्) or 'd' (द्) is followed by 'j' (ज्) or 'jh' (झ्), the preceding 't/d' assimilates into 'j' (ज्).
aiDeepSolution.trick: In 'Ujjwal', both 'j' letters are half (consonant cluster j + j + v + l). This is a frequent BPSC question in both Sandhi and orthography (spelling test).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Students often pick 'Ud + Jwal' due to colloquial Hindi variations, but according to Paninian Sanskrit grammar and official BPSC answer keys, 'Ut' is the standard prefix.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which type of compound (Samas) is present in the compound word 'Yathashakti' (यथाशक्ति)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Yathashakti' is an example of Avyayibhav Samas.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Avyayibhav Samas: A compound where the initial constituent is an Indeclinable/Prefix (Avyaya) and is the principal element, causing the whole compound to function adverbially.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Look for prefixes like 'Yatha-', 'Prati-', 'Be-', 'Ba-', 'Bhar-', 'Anu-'. Yathashakti literally translates to 'according to one's capacity'.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Tatpurush involves elision of case endings (Karak), whereas here 'Yatha' is an indeclinable modifier.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which of the following spellings is orthographically correct in Hindi?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The authentic feminine form of 'Kavi' is 'Kavayitri' (कवयित्री).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Feminine noun formation: In Hindi/Sanskrit, the feminine counterpart of Kavi is derived as Kav + ayitri, not Kavi + yatri.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Remember the syllable pattern: Ka - va - yi - tree (no vowel mark on 'va').
aiDeepSolution.trap: Most candidates intuitively place a short 'i' on 'v' (*Kaviyatri), which is an erroneous hypercorrection.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the correct verb to fill in the blank:
'Neither the teacher nor the students _______ present in the seminar yesterday.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The grammatically correct verb is 'were'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rule of Proximity: When two subjects are connected by correlative conjunctions 'Neither...nor' or 'Either...or', the finite verb agrees in number and person with the closest subject.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Identify the noun adjacent to the blank: 'students' (plural) -> requires plural past verb 'were' (time marker is 'yesterday').
aiDeepSolution.trap: If the sentence were inverted ('Neither the students nor the teacher...'), the verb would be singular ('was'). Here 'students' governs the verb.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate article to fill in the blank:
'He is _______ European scholar whom we met in Patna.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct indefinite article is 'a'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Indefinite article choice ('a' vs 'an') is strictly determined by the initial phonetic sound of the following word, not the orthographic letter. 'European' begins with the consonant glide /juː/ (like 'you').
aiDeepSolution.trick: Words like 'a European', 'a university', 'a unicorn', 'a one-rupee note' all take 'a' because they begin with consonant phonemes /j/ or /w/.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not mechanically pick 'an' merely because the word opens with vowel letter 'E'.

questions.subject: National Movement
questions.question: Who led the rebellion in Patna city on 3rd July 1857 during the Great Revolt of 1857?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Patna uprising of 3rd July 1857 was led by bookseller Peer Ali Khan.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Peer Ali Khan, a bookseller in Patna, mobilized the masses and attacked the colonial administration, killing British opium agent Dr. R. Lyell. Commissioner William Tayler executed Peer Ali along with his associates.
aiDeepSolution.trick: P for Patna = Peer Ali. Veer Kunwar Singh led the rebellion in Jagdishpur (Bhojpur / Shahabad).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Students frequently rush to mark Kunwar Singh, overlooking that the question specifically specifies 'Patna city'.

questions.subject: Champaran Satyagraha
questions.question: Who persuaded and invited Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran at the Lucknow Congress Session of 1916?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Peasant leader Rajkumar Shukla invited Mahatma Gandhi.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rajkumar Shukla, an indigo farmer from Murli Bharhawa village in Champaran, met Gandhi at the 1916 Lucknow Congress and persistently followed him to Kanpur and Kolkata until Gandhi agreed to visit Bihar in April 1917.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Shukla was described by Gandhi in his autobiography as 'resolute and determined'.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Brajkishore Prasad joined Gandhi's inquiry team after his arrival in Bihar; the invitation was exclusively initiated by Shukla.

questions.subject: Champaran Satyagraha
questions.question: Following the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), what percentage of illegally extorted dues did the European indigo planters agree to refund to the peasants upon the Champaran Agrarian Committee's recommendation?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: European planters agreed to refund 25% of the extorted money.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Champaran Agrarian Committee (which included Gandhi) abolished the oppressive Tinkathia system. The planters offered a 25% refund, which Gandhi accepted because it shattered the psychological myth of planter prestige and British invincibility.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Tinkathia = 3/20th part of land. Extorted money refund = exactly 25% (one-fourth).
aiDeepSolution.trap: A common distractor assumption is 50% or 100%, but the historical compromise was exactly 25%.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: In which district does the Ganga River first enter the territory of Bihar from Uttar Pradesh?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Ganga enters Bihar near Chausa in Buxar district.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Ganga flows for 445 km through Bihar, entering near Chausa in Buxar and exiting at Bhagalpur/Katihar into West Bengal. It touches 12 districts in Bihar.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Associate with the historic Battle of Chausa (1539, Sher Shah vs Humayun) situated on the banks of Ganga in Buxar.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Bhojpur lies downstream from Buxar; Buxar is the primary entry point.

questions.subject: Bihar Rivers
questions.question: Which river of Bihar is notoriously called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent course shifts and devastating floods, joining the Ganga at Kursela (Katihar)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Kosi River is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Originating in Nepal and Tibet as Saptakoshi, the Kosi carries enormous silt loads that block its bed, causing it to shift over 120 km westwards over the last 250 years. It merges with Ganga at Kursela in Katihar.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Sorrow of Bihar = Kosi (merges at Kursela).
aiDeepSolution.trap: The Burhi Gandak has the fastest discharge velocity, but course shifting and catastrophic flooding belong to the Kosi.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which specific endocrine cells in which human gland secrete the hormone Insulin?
options: Beta (β) cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the Pancreas
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Beta (β) cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the Pancreas secrete Insulin.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Pancreas is a heterocrine (mixed) gland. Its endocrine tissue, the Islets of Langerhans, consists of Alpha cells (Glucagon) and Beta cells (Insulin). Insulin facilitates glucose uptake and stimulates glycogenesis.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Beta cells = Insulin (lowers blood sugar). Alpha cells = Glucagon (raises blood sugar).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Kupffer cells are specialized macrophages residing in the liver, not hormone-secreting endocrine cells.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: When white light passes through a glass triangular prism, which spectral colour undergoes the minimum deviation and minimum scattering?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Red light suffers minimum deviation and scattering.

aiDeepSolution.concept: According to Rayleigh Scattering ($I \propto 1/\lambda^4$), scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength. Red light has the longest visible wavelength (approx. 700 nm), smallest refractive index in glass, and hence minimum deviation ($\\delta = (\mu - 1)A$).
aiDeepSolution.trick: VIBGYOR: Violet has maximum deviation; Red has minimum deviation.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Violet has maximum scattering and maximum refractive index; the question asks for MINIMUM.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Determine the next term in the arithmetic-square progression sequence: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The next term in the sequence is 37.

aiDeepSolution.trick: Sequence of differences is consecutive odd numbers: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.
aiDeepSolution.trap: 35 is $6^2 - 1$, which candidates mistakenly pick by reversing the sign.

questions.subject: Mathematics (6-8)
questions.question: If the HCF and LCM of two positive integers are 12 and 144 respectively, and one of the integers is 36, what is the value of the other integer?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The second integer is 48.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic property for two positive integers: $\text{HCF}(a, b) \times \text{LCM}(a, b) = a \times b$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Calculation: $12 \times 144 = 36 \times b \implies b = \frac{12 \times 144}{36} = \frac{144}{3} = 48$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: This product formula holds strictly for two numbers only; do not attempt for three numbers without modification.

questions.subject: Mathematics (6-8)
questions.source: Bihar SCERT Class 6 & BPSC TRE 1.0 PYQ
questions.question: If the 6-digit number 5432k7 is completely divisible by 9, what must be the single-digit value of 'k'?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The value of digit k is 6.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Divisibility Rule of 9: A number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of its constituent digits is a multiple of 9.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Sum of digits: $5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + k + 7 = 21 + k$. The next multiple of 9 after 21 is 27. Therefore, $21 + k = 27 \implies k = 6$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse divisibility of 9 with divisibility of 3 ($k=0, 3, 6, 9$ work for 3, but only $k=6$ works for 9).

questions.subject: Mathematics (6-8)
questions.question: What is the product of the additive inverse and the multiplicative inverse of the rational number -7/19?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The product is -1.

aiDeepSolution.concept: For any non-zero rational number $x$: Additive Inverse = $-x$; Multiplicative Inverse (reciprocal) = $1/x$. Their product is $(-x) \times (1/x) = -1$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Universal Property: The product of the additive inverse and multiplicative inverse of ANY non-zero number is ALWAYS -1.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates calculate $(7/19) \times (-19/7) = -1$. Do not lose the negative sign.

questions.subject: Mathematics (6-8)
questions.question: Evaluate the exponential numerical expression: $(1/2)^{-2} + (1/3)^{-2} + (1/4)^{-2}$
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The evaluated value is 29.

aiDeepSolution.trick: Direct calculation: $4 + 9 + 16 = 29$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Option C (61/144) is the result of $(1/4 + 1/9 + 1/16)$, where the negative exponent is erroneously ignored.

questions.subject: Science (Physics)
questions.question: Two plane mirrors are inclined to each other at an angle of 60°. How many distinct images of an object placed symmetrically between them will be formed?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Exactly 5 images will be formed.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Image formation formula by inclined mirrors: $m = 360^\circ / \theta$. Here $m = 360 / 60 = 6$. Since $m$ is an EVEN integer, number of images $n = m - 1 = 6 - 1 = 5$ (regardless of position).
aiDeepSolution.trick: If $360/\theta$ is even, subtract 1: $6 - 1 = 5$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often forget the '-1' subtraction and incorrectly choose 6.

questions.subject: Science (Biology)
questions.question: Which combination of chemical reagents is used to test for the presence of proteins in food, and what positive colour reaction confirms it?
options: Copper sulphate solution and Caustic soda (Violet colouration)
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Copper sulphate and Caustic soda produce a violet colour, confirming proteins (Biuret test).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Biuret test for peptide bonds: In an alkaline medium (Caustic soda / NaOH), Copper(II) ions ($CuSO_4$) chelate with peptide nitrogen atoms to form a violet/purple complex.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Iodine = Starch (Blue-Black). Biuret ($CuSO_4 + NaOH$) = Protein (Violet).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Option A is the diagnostic test for carbohydrates (starch), not proteins.

questions.subject: Science (Biology)
questions.question: Which of the following essential vitamins is water-soluble in human nutrition?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is water-soluble.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vitamins are classified into: Fat-soluble (Vitamins K, E, D, A) and Water-soluble (Vitamin B-complex and Vitamin C / Ascorbic acid). Water-soluble vitamins are readily excreted in urine and must be supplied regularly.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Mnemonic: 'KEDA' are fat-soluble. 'B and C' dissolve in water.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse Vitamin D (fat-soluble) with Vitamin C.

questions.subject: Science (Physics)
questions.source: Bihar SCERT Class 7 & BPSC TRE 1.0 PYQ
questions.question: Which optical mirror is installed as a rear-view mirror in motor vehicles to provide a wide field of view?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images of distant objects, and curve outwards, giving the driver a significantly wider field of view than a plane mirror.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Convex = Diverging mirror = Erect diminished image + Wide panorama.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Concave mirrors produce inverted images for distant objects, making them unusable as rear-view mirrors.

questions.subject: Science (Biology)
questions.question: Scurvy is a clinical deficiency disease caused by the prolonged lack of which vitamin in the human diet?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) is an essential cofactor for collagen synthesis. Deficiency leads to fragile blood capillaries, bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and scurvy.
aiDeepSolution.trick: C for Citrus = C for Ascorbic acid = C for Scurvy prevention.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi; Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets.

questions.subject: Science (Physics)
questions.question: What is the nature and size of the image formed by a concave spherical mirror when an object is placed between its Principal Focus (F) and Pole (P)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The image is virtual, erect, and magnified, formed behind the mirror.

aiDeepSolution.concept: This is the single exceptional case for concave mirrors. When the object is inside the focal length ($u < f$), the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror, creating a virtual, upright, and magnified image (utilized in shaving/dentist mirrors).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Inside Focus = Virtual and Magnified. Beyond Focus = Real and Inverted.
aiDeepSolution.trap: All other positions for concave mirrors yield REAL and INVERTED images; this is the only virtual case.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.question: According to Euclid's Division Lemma, for any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique whole numbers q and r such that $a = bq + r$. What is the mandatory condition on remainder r?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The remainder must satisfy $0 \le r < b$.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Euclid's Division Lemma formalizes the long division algorithm: the remainder can be zero or strictly positive, but it MUST be strictly smaller than the divisor $b$. If $r = b$, the quotient increases by 1.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Strict inequality at the upper bound: $0 \le r < b$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Option C includes $r \le b$, which is invalid because a remainder can never equal the divisor.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.question: After how many decimal places will the decimal expansion of the rational number 13/1250 terminate?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The decimal expansion terminates after 4 decimal places.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Let $x = p/q$ in simplest terms. If $q = 2^n \cdot 5^m$, the decimal terminates after $\max(n, m)$ places. Here $1250 = 2^1 \times 5^4$. The powers are $n=1, m=4$. $\max(1, 4) = 4$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Prime factorize denominator: $1250 = 2 \times 625 = 2^1 \times 5^4$. Highest exponent is 4 -> terminates in 4 decimal places ($13/1250 = 0.0104$).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not divide manually in exam conditions; apply the $\max(n, m)$ exponent rule directly.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.question: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial $P(x) = 2x^2 - 5x + 7$, what is the exact numerical value of $(1/\alpha + 1/\beta)$?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The value of $(1/\alpha + 1/\beta)$ is 5/7.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Sum of roots $\alpha + \beta = -b/a = -(-5)/2 = 5/2$. Product of roots $\alpha\beta = c/a = 7/2$. Then $1/\alpha + 1/\beta = (\alpha + \beta)/(\alpha\beta) = (5/2)/(7/2) = 5/7$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Direct BPSC Shortcut: $1/\alpha + 1/\beta = -b/c = -(-5)/7 = 5/7$. Solve in 3 seconds!
aiDeepSolution.trap: Sign error: candidates forget the leading minus in $-b/c$ and answer $-5/7$.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.source: NCERT Exemplar & BPSC TRE 2.0 Exact PYQ
questions.question: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial $x^2 + 99x + 127$, what are the algebraic signs of both zeroes?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Both zeroes are strictly negative.

aiDeepSolution.concept: For $ax^2 + bx + c$, if $a, b, c > 0$: Product $\alpha\beta = c/a = 127/1 > 0$ implies both roots have the same sign. Sum $\alpha + \beta = -b/a = -99 < 0$ implies both must be negative.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Rule: If all coefficients of a quadratic polynomial are positive, both roots MUST be negative.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not solve the discriminant or use quadratic formula; inspect signs of sum and product.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.question: If one of the zeroes of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$ is equal to 0, what is the product of the other two zeroes?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The product of the other two zeroes is c/a.

aiDeepSolution.concept: In a cubic polynomial with roots $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$, the sum of pairwise products is $\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = c/a$. If $\gamma = 0$, then $\alpha\beta + 0 + 0 = c/a \implies \alpha\beta = c/a$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Set $\gamma = 0$ in $\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = c/a$ -> $\alpha\beta = c/a$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse with the product of all three roots $\alpha\beta\gamma = -d/a$.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding real numbers:
1. The sum of a rational and an irrational number is always irrational.
2. The product of two irrational numbers is always irrational.
3. Every real number is either rational or irrational.
Which of the above statements is/are mathematically TRUE?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are true; Statement 2 is false.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Statement 1 is TRUE (Rational + Irrational = Irrational). Statement 2 is FALSE: e.g. $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2} = 2$ (rational) or $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{6}$ (irrational). Statement 3 is TRUE: $\mathbb{R} = \mathbb{Q} \cup \mathbb{Q}'$.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Counterexample for statement 2: $(\sqrt{3}) \times (\sqrt{3}) = 3$ (rational). Thus 2 is false.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Believing irrational numbers are closed under multiplication is a classic mathematical trap.

questions.subject: Mathematics (9-10)
questions.source: NCERT Class 9 Polynomials & BPSC TRE 2.0 PYQ
questions.question: When the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 3$ is divided by $(x - 2)$, what is the remainder obtained according to the Remainder Theorem?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The remainder is 3.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Remainder Theorem: When polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $(x - a)$, the remainder is simply $P(a)$. Here $a = 2$.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Arithmetic error while evaluating signs of terms.
